subject: Novaforge MSA redlines — indemnity carve / defend vs reimburse
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@novaforge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Ethan Murray <ethan.murray@novaforge.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novaforge MSA — redlines attached (IP indemnity)

Karthik,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Attached are Novaforge's current redlines to the MSA — please focus on the indemnity section. Two core asks from our side:

1) Broad third-party IP indemnity that covers claims arising from customer-facing outputs (they want defend + indemnify for direct claims).
2) Narrow carveouts for training-data allegations are not acceptable to them unless we provide an alternate mitigation (e.g., insurance).

Procurement (cc'd) asked for an ETA on whether Redwood can accept a defend obligation or whether you will insist on a reimbursement model plus insurance/escrow. Please route to legal if needed.

Attachment: Novaforge_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf

Sara Patel
General Counsel
Novaforge, Inc.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@novaforge.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novaforge MSA — redlines attached (IP indemnity)

Sara — thanks, got the packet. Looping in Kim (legal) and Ben (AE) to triage. Quick summary from our side so everyone has context:

- We can accept a defend obligation for third-party infringement where the claim relates to our model weights or runtime service (classic third-party IP claims), but there are carve points our counsel will ask for:
  * Exclude claims that relate solely to customer-supplied prompts or customer-hosted derivative models.
  * Require timely notice and the ability for Redwood to control defense (or reasonable coordination with customer counsel).

- For model-output attribution / training-data allegations Novaforge is asking us to accept broader risk. Our current posture is: we will not assume open-ended training-data exposure without either (i) insurance that covers those claims, or (ii) a narrowly-tailored escrow/indemnity pool tied to order-form spend.

Kim, can you propose precise language that preserves defend but limits scope to "third-party claims alleging direct infringement of a third party's IP by the Service," and that excludes outputs tied to Customer prompts/derivatives? Also include an evidence checklist and notice timing we can provide to Novaforge to make this palatable.

Ben — can you push back a bit on the insurance ask if you think Novaforge will accept an escrow or higher cap tied to the order form? If not, we'll need to escalate for exec approval.

Attachment: RWF_defend_vs_reimburse_markdown.docx

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novaforge MSA — redlines attached (IP indemnity)

Karthik/Ben — reviewed. High-level legal guidance and draft redline suggestions below. I'm pasting the key proposed replacement for the indemnity clause and an evidence checklist we recommend providing to Novaforge (short, operational, makes defense realistic).

Proposed approach (concise):
- Keep "Right to Defend" language but narrow the trigger to "claims alleging direct infringement of a third party's issued copyright or patent by use of the Service as delivered by Redwood."
- Add explicit carveout for Customer-generated prompts, Customer-hosted fine-tuned models, and Customer data where Customer had exclusive control.
- Cap: tie to the Order Form's annual spend or a fixed aggregate cap (we propose "the greater of 1x annual recurring fees or $1M").
- Insurance/escrow: present as alternative remediation. If customer insists on training-data exposures, offer a time-limited proof plan (90 days) where Novaforge supplies incident evidence and Redwood commits to a remediation roadmap; insurance required only if claim arises from third-party allegation of training-data provenance (rare).

Evidence checklist (attachment):
- Notice of claim (copy of complaint or demand)
- Identification of the allegedly infringed work and claimant contact
- Reproduction sample (if available) and evidence showing it was generated during the customer's session (timestamp, API key)
- Any customer materials asserting ownership/derivation

These items make it much easier for us to accept defend without open-ended risk. If Ben thinks procurement will balk at a $1M floor, we can convert to a multi-tier cap tied to committed spend.

Attachment: evidence_checklist.xlsx

Kim
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Pat Harper <pat.harper@slawfirm.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@novaforge.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novaforge MSA — redlines attached (IP indemnity)

Karthik/Sara/Kim — my client Novaforge asked me to provide some practical redline notes. Two points from their side:

1) Novaforge will not accept a cap that effectively wipes out recoverability for a medium-sized claim — they asked us to consider a split cap (lower cap for direct infringement claims, higher for output-related statutory damages), or a deductible to demonstrate good faith.

2) On carveouts: Novaforge is willing to accept reasonable customer-responsibility language for prompts, but only where the provider can actually demonstrate causation. They ask for explicit discovery rights to obtain Redwood logs if they pursue a defense.

I've attached our suggested markup (comments), which narrows the provider carveouts but also adds an obligation for Redwood to preserve and produce relevant logs when a claim is asserted.

Attachment: PatHarper_redline_notes.docx

Best,
Pat Harper
Partner, S&L LLP (outside counsel to Novaforge)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novaforge MSA — redlines attached (IP indemnity)

Team — quick internal plan and asks before we reply to Novaforge:

1) Ben: please draft a two-step commercial concession we can offer in the next email — (A) defense for classic third-party IP claims with a cap equal to the greater of 1x ARR or $1M, (B) a conditional escalation path if Novaforge insists on broader training-data exposure (escalate to revenue ops + exec review for insurance or escrow). Put this in the email as an explicit trade (defend + limited cap vs. insurance/escrow ask).

2) Kim: include the evidence checklist as a collateral (we can attach to the reply) and prepare the redline language that: (i) preserves Redwood's right to control defense, (ii) requires timely notice, and (iii) excludes customer prompts-derived claims unless customer cannot produce logs showing derivation. Also prepare a short set of log-preservation commitments (what we can provide without compromising other customers).

3) I'll coordinate with Product to confirm what logs we can reasonably produce (timestamps, API key hash, model id) and with Ops on retention windows. We should avoid promising long-term log retention without a contract term.

Next step: Ben to send a single reply to Sara/Ethan/Pat tomorrow morning with the two-step concession + attached evidence checklist and our redline excerpt. Kim, plan to include your redline as a follow-up if they push on scope.
